review_output.summary: The command-parsing loop runs to i <= argc and checks `sds_args[i][0]` whenever i == start, before checking i == argc. That reads past the end of the argc-sized sds_args array.
review_output.failure_scenario: `valkey-benchmark SET a b \;` (a trailing ';' separator): at i=3 the ';' sets start=4, then at i=4 (== argc == start) the code dereferences sds_args[4], an out-of-bounds heap read and a possible crash. The same happens when argc is 0 after --stdin realloc edge cases, since getSdsArrayFromArgv allocates exactly argc slots.

review_output.summary: The custom-command exit path frees only config.server_config. In cluster mode the per-node `server_config` objects (and the cluster nodes) are never freed, because freeClusterNodes() is not called on either exit path of main.
review_output.failure_scenario: `valkey-benchmark --cluster SET k v`: each node's serverConfig from getServerConfig (line 1872) leaks at exit, and ASan/valgrind runs report leaked sds save/appendonly strings per node.

review_output.summary: The default-suite exit path has the same problem: it frees config.server_config but never the cluster nodes' server_config.
review_output.failure_scenario: `valkey-benchmark --cluster -t set`: the node serverConfig objects and node structs leak at exit, and the renamed field is not covered by any cleanup.

review_output.summary: The early `return 0` for custom commands skips `freeCliConnInfo(config.conn_info)` and `zfree(data)`-style cleanup that the default-suite path does at line 2204, so the two exit paths are inconsistent.
review_output.failure_scenario: `valkey-benchmark -a pass SET k v` under a leak checker: conn_info hostip/auth/user strings are reported as leaked, while the default suite path frees them.

review_output.summary: Non-cluster mode prints `config.server_config->save` directly, but cluster mode maps an empty save to "NONE" (line 894). Standalone output shows an empty value when persistence is disabled.
review_output.failure_scenario: Server with `save ""`: the standalone report prints `host configuration "save": ` (blank), while the cluster report prints `save: NONE` for the same config. Output is inconsistent and misleading.

review_output.summary: freeClusterNode frees slots and server_config but not `node->updated_slots`, which updateClusterSlotsConfiguration allocates (line 1276).
review_output.failure_scenario: A slot update fills node->updated_slots, then fetchClusterConfiguration fails or re-runs and calls freeClusterNodes (line 1185) before the swap at line 1299. The CLUSTER_SLOTS*sizeof(int) buffer leaks.
